name: Mid-century eyewear
summary: The glasses and sun glasses of the years after 1937. Frames in celluloid and acetate took the cat-eye, browline and round panto shapes, beside the thin gold-filled aviator. Glasses became a fashion item and not only a medical aid.

philosophy.core_thesis: Glasses are a part of the face, and the frame gives the wearer a character.
design_principles: Cut the frame in plastic, 3 to 5 mm thick, with a keyhole or a flat bridge.
Raise the outer corner of the lens by 10 to 20 degrees for the cat-eye.
Join a heavy brow bar of plastic to a thin metal rim for the browline.
Choose a tortoiseshell pattern or a solid colour in the plastic.
Set rhinestones or metal studs in the upper corner of a ladies' frame.
Fix the temples with 5-barrel hinges on a core wire.
Make the lens 48 to 54 mm wide.
Offer one frame in many colours, so that the wearer owns more than one pair.
anti_patterns: Rimless frames with no visible border
Thin titanium wire with a sports finish

silhouette.shape: A pair of lenses in a frame that sweeps up at the outer edge, or sits heavy on the brow.
silhouette.line: A strong top line that follows the brow, and a lower rim that curves away.
silhouette.fit: The frame sits on the bridge of the nose, with the temples running straight back over the ears.
silhouette.proportion: Lens 48–54 mm wide; bridge 16–22 mm; temple 135–145 mm; cat-eye tip 10–20 degrees above the horizontal.
rules: Lift the outer corner, so that the eye looks wider and longer.
Make the top of the frame heavier than the bottom.
Keep the bridge low and the temples slim.
Add detail only at the corner: a stud, a stone or a metal tip.

fabrics.rule: Use a plastic that polishes to a deep gloss and takes a tortoiseshell pattern, and a thin gold-filled or steel wire for metal frames.

methods: frame cut from laminated acetate sheet
metal rim joined to a plastic brow bar
construction.closures: Temple arms on riveted hinges; a nose pad of plastic or of metal.
construction.details: Rhinestone studs, a keyhole bridge, a metal brow rod and a maker's mark on the temple.

surface.pattern: A tortoiseshell mottle, a solid colour or a laminate of two colours: black over pink or clear.
surface.gloss: Polished plastic at 90–100 GU; brushed steel at 20–35 GU.
surface.wear: A frame yellows and scratches with age; a clean, glossy frame is the aim, and a collector prizes an unworn pair.

palette.strategy: A warm tortoiseshell or black frame as the base, with a pastel or a metal as an accent.

making.scale: Optical factories made frames in the thousands; small shops cut limited runs by hand.
making.signs: A deep, even polish, flush hinges and studs set without a gap.

pieces.form: Cat-eye frame with raised corners and rhinestone studs
Browline frame: a heavy plastic brow bar over a thin metal rim
Round panto frame in a tortoiseshell pattern, in celluloid
Teardrop aviator in thin gold-filled wire
Sun glasses with a brushed steel frame and bayonet temples

positive: studio portrait of a woman in glasses

evidence.title: 1950sGlasses.jpg
evidence.credit: Nabokov (talk). Required citation is: "Photo by Tom Oates, 2009".

emotion.target_response: A sense of wit and of sharp attention: the frame gives the face a clear, confident line.

use_cases: a costume brief for a 1950s film
a fashion image prompt for 1950s eyewear
avoid_when: the brief is sports or safety eyewear
the brief wants a minimal rimless frame

modifiers.how: Keep the thin lines, set stones along the top rim and use black with silver.
Round the lens, thin the frame and pick a bright solid colour.

ornament_level.note: A plain frame has no studs; a ladies' cat-eye carries rhinestones.
